Atala is a loveless state of lust, self-indulgence, and intoxicating hypnotic fantasy in which the mind demands constant stimulation, variety, novelty, and sensory expansion to avoid facing the inner emptiness caused by lack of knowledge of the unborn wholeness of your innermost nature, ananda. Without Self knowledge you are trapped by the projection that sense objects, which are value neutral contain the blissful love you crave.
Vitala is a conceited, refined mind trapped by aesthetic beauty, intellectual superiority, and a golden self-image born of a failure to appreciate the one Self’s unborn wholeness.
Sutala is populated with righteous, seemingly humble but proud people with religious and spiritual inclinations. Once their animal instincts are mastered these self-appointed do-gooders fall in love with their own benign egos. Blessed with predominately respectable sattvic dispositions, they tend to be anxiety-free and small self-satisfied. Usually, they feel so “blessed” they are unable to see, much less surrender, unseemly remaining ego remnants. This realm is a golden sattvic chain binding the soul to the denial that always accompanies projections.

Talatala is a threshold state that marks the transition from egoic/personality traps into rationalized self-deception, a psyche that creates intricate cognitive illusions and defense mechanisms to protect itself from the truth of the ever-free Self. It is entrapment in a matrix of logic where everything is explained, optimized, and engineered, entirely devoid of spontaneity, genuine spiritual life, and love.

It is ruled by Maya as a brilliant architect and engineer in the form of miraculous technology and sacred geometry... People in this cohort seek to solve deep existential yearnings with ideas, planning, efficiency, and material designs.

Sacred geometry wielded by a competent teacher can open the door beyond intellectual self-sufficiency.

Mahatala represents a shift into deeper, primal layers of the subterranean psyche ruled by large eagle-fearing serpents (nagas) with many hoods whose fundamental organizing principle is anger... The mind suffers chronic anxiety, paranoia, hyper-vigilance, and defensive rage. Rage masks a vulnerable mind addicted to indignation because anger feels more powerful than fear.
Pātala (here labeled Dog-Eat-Dog Survival) extends the deeper shadow. It is pure tamoguna at the bottom of the Macrocosmic Causal Body... a sunless world illuminated by artificial light from the naga’s bejewelled hoods. The psyche feels self-sufficient and complete, living by its own “lights.”
Rasātala: This “Look but Don’t Touch” realm is a frustrating hellscape. The inhabitants are immensely powerful and cruel, living amid gem-lit opulence, yet their desire to loot is perpetually checked by the golden Sudarśana Cakra of Viṣṇu. Sufficient sattva arises that they realize chasing gold is zero-sum; for fear of the downside they only look but don’t touch.
Reflected Awareness (panel 8) points toward the pure, unconditioned awareness that is the true nature of the Self. It is the light that illuminates all the lower realms yet remains untouched by them - the ever-present I that is whole and complete.
Sheshanaga, the cosmic serpent with infinite heads…unmanifest, ground-level divinity...supports the entire universe. The lowest realm is the "place" where the apparent reality seemingly touches the divine substratum and where egoic strategies don’t work. It is the doorway to the ever-free non-dual world, existence shining as unborn whole and complete awareness experienced always as the ever-present I.
